ACMD 502.description: Becoming a Leader in Academic Medicine. Current approaches to leadership within the context of academic medicine and health professions education, leadership styles, emotional intelligence, critical reflection, well-being and personal leadership journeys.

ACMD 503.description: Leading Change in Academic Medical Centers. Developing skills for promoting programs within health professions education; teams and teamwork, organizational change, conflict resolution, crucial conversations, non-violent communication, negotiation and teaching leadership.

lectures.instructor: Jerry Gates; Julie Nyquist; Samuel Yanofsky

ACMD 511.description: Instructional Design in Academic Medicine and Health. Focuses on Instructional Design for Health Professions Education. Content includes learning principles, teaching methods, session development, assessment techniques and designing curricula (Plan, Implement, Evaluate, Disseminate).

ACMD 512.description: Competencies in Academic Medicine and Health. Learning theory, teaching methods, assessment techniques related to acquisition and reinforcement of competencies related to patient care, practice based learning and improvement and systems-based practice.

ACMD 591.description: Designing Research on Innovations in Academic Medicine. Introduction to design and scholarly review of innovations in health professions education; needs assessment, problem selection, use of research methods to study an innovation.

ACMD 592.description: Implementing Research on Innovation in Academic Medicine. Mentored research on an innovation in academic medicine, qualitative and qualitative methods, and producing a formal written research report:

ACMD 598.description: Fieldwork: Designing Innovations for the Health Professions. Individual projects designing curricular or other innovations for an individual program or specialty as an extension of program concepts or deepening the capstone experience.

ACMD 621.description: Capstone Portfolio for the Master of Academic Medicine. Role of portfolios for teachers and learners; develop a personal capstone portfolio that represents each learners accomplishment of the core competencies of the MACM program.

ACCT 370.description: External Financial Reporting Issues. Understanding of decision-making, problem solving, and research skills as a supplement to financial accounting knowledge for accounting professionals.

ACCT 371.description: Introduction to Accounting Systems. Understanding of technology and controls needed to capture data used by professionals in financial and managerial accounting, auditing and taxation.

ACCT 410.description: Foundations of Accounting. Non-technical presentation of accounting for users of accounting information; introduction to financial and managerial accounting. Not open to students with course credits in accounting. Not available for unit or course credit toward a degree in Accounting or Business.

ACCT 416.description: Financial Statement Analysis. Analysis of corporate financial reports from a decision-maker's perspective.

ACCT 430.description: Accounting Ethics. Theoretical knowledge and practical application accountants need to identify ethical issues and reconcile conflicts among competing stakeholders' interests in all major areas of accounting practice.

ACCT 451.description: Tax Analysis with Data Analytics. Capabilities to identify and analyze relevant tax issues; apply research tools to find solutions and provide alternate approaches using data analytics.   Duplicates credit in the former ACCT 374 and the former ACCT 474.

ACCT 456.description: Auditing with Data Analytics. Auditing with data analytics from the perspective of management    and other users of financial statements including external         auditors and assurance professionals.  Duplicates credit in the    former ACCT 373 and the former ACCT 473.

ACCT 470.description: Advanced External Financial Reporting Issues. Develop capabilities to identify and resolve advanced external financial reporting challenges, focusing primarily on operating, financing, and investing activities of business enterprises.

ACCT 490.description: Directed Research. Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.

ACCT 526.description: Global Accounting Experience. Cross-border transactions in the global economy examining accounting, legal, and tax environments, economic and political systems, and cultural differences. Includes international travel to selected region.

ACCT 528.description: Fair Value Accounting: GAAP, IFRS and Emerging Issues. Case study approach to explore fair value issues in accounting; research and analysis of causes of valuation differences.

ACCT 532.description: Financial Accounting for Mergers and Acquisitions. Practical problems in accounting for business combinations. Consolidated financial statements: fair value, acquisition and equity basis accounting. Duplicates credit in former ACCT 582.

ACCT 533.description: Mergers and Acquisitions: Tax Planning and Strategy. Tax planning and strategy in corporate restructuring including mergers, acquisitions, and divestitures.  Tax background not required to be successful in this course.  Duplicates credit in former ACCT 582.

ACCT 540.description: AI and Emerging Technologies in Accounting and Auditing. Investigate the future of data and analytics and emerging technologies in accounting and business to facilitate innovation and prediction.

ACCT 542.description: Fraud Analytics in the Audit. Understanding/identifying fraud risk from an auditor's perspective; development of an analytics skillset to detect financial fraud risk.

ACCT 548.description: IT Audit and Data Applications. Exploration of the role systems play in organizations, the technology that supports these systems and issues relating to technology risk, system/application security and system review/audit.

ACCT 551T.description: Taxation of Partnerships. Federal taxation of flow-through entities including partnerships, limited liability partnerships (LLPs), and limited liability companies (LLCs).

ACCT 557.description: Advanced Financial Statement Auditing Topics. Advanced coverage of topics in financial statement auditing  including market effects of auditing, auditor litigation and  client acceptance, errors and fraud, analytical procedures, and  going-concern assessment.

ACCT 559.description: Strategy and Operations Through CFO Lens. Examination of strategic objectives and operations within specific industries and companies. Chief Financial Officers present how they view the business as a whole and measure performance effectively.

ACCT 561T.description: Income Tax of Corporations and Their Shareholders. Concepts and principles governing the taxation of corporations and their shareholders; the effect of taxes on corporate formation, capital structure, distributions, and liquidations.

ACCT 568T.description: International Taxation. Taxation of cross-border transactions of U.S. citizens and corporations and of U.S. source income of foreign persons and corporations; planning for organization of international operations under the tax laws.

ACCT 570T.description: State and Local Tax Concepts. State income taxes; property tax; other state and local taxes; the effect of state and local taxes on multistate operations.

ACCT 571T.description: Taxation of Business Owners and High Net-Worth Individuals. Application of tax law in areas of compensation planning, investment planning, tax shelters, and current developments relating to the individual taxpayer.

ACCT 580T.description: Tax Accounting Methods. Concepts governing timing of recognition of income and deductions for income tax purposes. Covers differences between GAAP and income tax accounting for all taxpayers.

ACCT 581.description: Financial Statement Analysis. Analysis of corporate financial reports from a decision-maker's perspective. This course is case-and-applications-oriented. Applications include credit analysis, equity valuation, and financial distress. Duplicates credit in ACCT 527.

ACCT 584.description: Family Wealth Preservation. Analysis of transfer of property during lifetime or at death from a tax saving perspective.

ACCT 589.description: Practicum. Experiential learning through practical training. Graded CR/NC.

ACCT 595.description: Internship in Accounting. Supervised on-the-job business experience in the field of Accounting. (Curricular Practical Training). Application required. Recommended preparation: Completion of required MAcc or MBT coursework. Graded CR/NC.

ACCT 611.description: Selected Topics in Accounting Research. Advanced seminar to address issues/topics covered in accounting research.

AME 201.description: Statics. Analysis of forces acting on particles and rigid bodies in static equilibrium; equivalent systems of forces; friction; centroids and moments of inertia; introduction to energy methods.

AME 204.description: Mechanics of Materials and Structures. Stress, strain and deflection of mechanical elements due to tension, shear, bending, or torsion; combined loads; plates, shells, statically indeterminate structures; strength-based design, trusses.

AME 208.description: Computational Methods in Engineering. Common tools for Aerospace and Mechanical engineers: vectors, matrices, fundamentals of python, data manipulation and analysis, statistics, data presentation, optimization, large data sets.

AME 261.description: Basic Flight Mechanics. Performance of flight vehicles; maximum speed, rate-of-climb, range, and endurance; basic stability and control, weight, and balance; computer exercises.

AME 291.description: Undergraduate Design Projects I. Analysis, design, fabrication, and evaluation of devices intended  for entry in local and national design competitions.  Intended for  lower division students or those with little prior project  experience.  Graded CR/NC.

AME 301.description: Dynamics. Reference frames and coordinate systems; relationships between forces, moments, power, linear/angular momentum, and energy for particles and rigid bodies; particle and rigid body systems.

AME 302A.description: Modeling and Analysis of Dynamic Systems. Mathematical modeling of constrained mechanical systems, transfer function formulation, state-space models, block diagram representation, time-domain open-loop systems response analysis; application to electrical circuits.

AME 302B.description: Modeling and Analysis of Dynamic Systems. Modeling and analysis of mechanical and combined dynamic systems; simple mechanisms; design-oriented approach to dynamic systems; system stability; approximation with lower-order systems, engineering applications.

AME 308.description: Computer-Aided Engineering. Introduction to the finite element method; practical application of computer analysis tools for structural analysis and design.

AME 309.description: Dynamics of Fluids. Fluid statics; conservation of mass, momentum, and energy in integral and differential form; applications. Laminar and turbulent pipe flow; compressible flow; potential flow over bodies.

AME 310.description: Engineering Thermodynamics I. Laws of thermodynamics applied to actual and perfect gases and vapors; energy concepts, processes, and applications; energy, entropy, and exergy analysis; power and refrigeration systems

AME 341B.description: Mechoptronics Laboratory. Coordinated laboratory and lecture sequence on aeromechanical instrumentation, test and measurement, integration of mechanical, optical and electronic components and technical communication.

AME 408.description: Computer-Aided Design of Mechanical Systems. Design of mechanical systems using advanced graphics techniques; computer-aided drafting, design optimization, elements of computer graphics, solids modeling; introduction to computer-aided manufacturing.

AME 409.description: Senior Design Project. Modelling, analysis, integration, layout and performance analysis of a mechanical system to meet the specified design requirements.

AME 415.description: Turbine Design and Analysis. Physics of turbine operation; design and analysis for the development of turbine hardware for propulsion and power generation.

AME 420.description: Engineering Vibrations I. The theory of free and forced vibrations with and without damping; systems with single and multiple degrees of freedom; solution methods; introduction to continuous systems.

AME 431.description: Heat Transfer. General principles underlying heat transfer by conduction, convection, and radiation; steady and transient conditions; heat exchangers.

AME 436.description: Automotive and Flight Propulsion. Analysis of combustion engines: reciprocating-piston, gas turbines, rockets. Tradeoffs compared to non-combustion sources. Ideal and non-ideal cycle analysis and performance evaluation; pollutant formation and remediation.

AME 441A.description: Senior Projects Laboratory. Team engineering design project to model, construct and test a physical principle or system. Complete industrial research project including proposal, design review, presentation, technical report.

AME 441B.description: Senior Projects Laboratory. Individual engineering projects designed and constructed to model and test a physical principle or system.

AME 443.description: Control Systems Laboratory. Practical measurement, analysis, and control of dynamic systems; system identification; linear control system design; simulation and verification of control system performance; and experimental controller implementation.

AME 451.description: Linear Control Systems I. Transform methods, block diagrams; transfer functions; stability; root-locus and frequency domain analysis and design; application to flight control, state space and multiloop systems.

AME 455.description: Introduction to Microelectromechanical Systems. Introduction to micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS); scaling effects; materials and structures in MEMS; MEMS sensing and actuation principles; microfabrication.

AME 460.description: Aerodynamic Theory. Basic relations describing the inviscid flow field about bodies and wings moving at subsonic and supersonic speeds.

AME 481.description: Aircraft Design. Aircraft design and analysis, design requirements and specifications; integration of structure, propulsion, control system, and aerodynamic configuration; performance analysis and prediction.

AME 486.description: Mechanics of Composite Materials for Modern Structures. Current and potential applications of composite materials including manufacturing methods; determining mechanical properties; failure analysis; and design, inspection, and repair considerations.

AME 490.description: Directed Research.  Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.

AME 491.description: Undergraduate Design Projects II. Analysis, design, fabrication, and evaluation of devices intended  for entry in local and national design competitions.  Intended for  students with prior project experience.  Upper division standing.   Graded CR/NC.

AME 501.description: Innovative Conceptual Design for New Product Development. A logic-based framework for conceptual design, including systematic concept generation and improvement, in innovative product developments.

AME 503.description: Advanced Mechanical Design. Specific problems and methods of analysis in mechanical systems design.

AME 504.description: Mechatronics Systems Engineering. Use of mechanical, electrical and computer engineering, math and computer science to design of high performance and sophisticated products and processes and systems involving mechatronics.

AME 508.description: Machine Learning and Computational Physics. Machine learning applications in computational physics and engineering; relationships between computational physics and ML algorithms; hybrid physics-informed ML prediction with tools for uncertainty quantification.

AME 509.description: Applied Elasticity. Cartesian tensors; kinematics of deformation, balance laws, and constitutive equations; variational principles; finite elasticity; plates and cylindrical shells; viscoelasticity; analytical and numerical solutions for elasticity.

AME 510.description: Advanced Computational Design and Manufacturing. Study concepts behind computational representations, algorithms and mathematical foundations, and their applications in computer-aided design and manufacturing. Develop hands-on computational skills in team projects.

AME 511.description: Compressible Gas Dynamics. Compressible flow equations; Rayleigh/Fanno flows; shock/expansion waves and interactions; potential flow, small disturbance theory and similarity; hypersonics; viscosity, high-temperature and radiation effects.

AME 513B.description: Fundamentals and Applications of Combustion. Advanced topics in combustion including analytical methods, stretch effects, stability, ignition and extinction of flames, plasma-assisted combustion, turbulence effects, detonations, and micropower generation.

AME 521.description: Engineering Vibrations II. Multi-degree of freedom systems; continuous systems; modal analysis. Beams, rods, membranes, plates, shells. Approximate methods; Galerkin, Rayleigh Ritz; assumed-mode, finite elements.

AME 522.description: Nonlinear Dynamical Systems, Vibrations, and Chaos. Flows on a line and circle; phase plane methods; bifurcation theory; limit cycle/relaxation oscillations; chaotic systems, one-dimensional maps, the Lorenz equations, fractals and strange attractors.

AME 526.description: Partial Differential Equations for Engineering Applications. Solving linear heat, wave, Laplace and Poisson equations, separation of variables and Fourier series, special functions, Fourier and Laplace transforms, characteristics, Greens functions, similarity solutions.

AME 529.description: Aircraft Structures Analysis. Stress Analysis. Linear Elasticity. Thin Plates. Finite Element Methods. Structural stability. Vibration of Continuous Systems. Emphasis on aerospace and aeronautical applications

AME 535B.description: Introduction to Computational Fluid Mechanics. Generalized curvilinear coordinates; grid generation; numerical    techniques for transonic and supersonic inviscid flows: boundary   layer flows; reduced Navier-Stokes equations; compressible and     incompressible viscous flows.  Recommended preparation: AME 511 or  AME 530a.

AME 544.description: Computer Control of Mechanical Systems.  Computer control as applied to machine tools, mechanical          manipulators, and other mechanical machinery; discrete time        controller design; microprocessor implementation of motion and     force control servos.

AME 549.description: Systems Architecting. Introduction to systems architecture in aerospace, electrical,     computer, and manufacturing systems emphasizing the conceptual and acceptance phases and using heuristics.

AME 550.description: Seminar in Aerospace and Mechanical Engineering. Recent developments and research in aerospace and mechanical engineering and related fields. Oral and written reports.

AME 552.description: Nonlinear Control Systems. Phase plane, describing function, applications to mechanical and aerospace systems. Lyapunov stability theory. Popov theorem. Circle criterion. Lyapunov redesign. Sliding mode control. Backstepping. Passivity.

AME 554.description: Additive Manufacturing Technologies. Overview and working principles of commonly used additive manufacturing processes; process models; process and material selection; cost estimation methods; current applications and future directions.

AME 560.description: Fatigue and Fracture. Behavior of materials under cyclic and static fatigue; plastic instability; life-time predictions; brittle and ductile fracture; crack propagation and plastic blunting.

AME 577.description: Survey of Energy and Power for a Sustainable Future. Power production includes conventional fossil fuels, synthetic fuels, hydroelectric, solar, wind, geothermal, biomass and nuclear. The environmental consequences of various energy sources are discussed.

AME 580.description: Computational Multiphysics Modeling in Engineering Science. Mathematical formulation and computational implementation of the partial differential equations governing coupled physical phenomena often treated separately; e.g., electro-chemo-thermo-fluid-solid mechanics.

AME 585.description: Aerospace Structures II. Finite element analysis of aerospace structures including heat transfer, joints, bellows, pressure vessels, flexible dynamics, random vibrations, repairs, buckling, fatigue/fracture and stress concentrations.

AME 588.description: Materials Selection. Materials selection in relationship to design and fabrication, economic considerations, methodology of selection, performance parameters; case studies.

AMST 101.description: Race and Class in Los Angeles. Analysis of race and the economic, political, gender, and social dimensions of contemporary Los Angeles including topics such as residential segregation, economic inequality, and city politics.

AMST 135.description: Peoples and Cultures of the Americas. An introduction to cultures and people in the Americas; the social, historical, economic and cultural formations that together make up the Latino/a American imaginary.

AMST 200.description: Introduction to American Studies and Ethnicity. Introduction to American studies and ethnic studies. Provides an overview of major theories, concepts, and issues.

AMST 204.description: Introduction to Native Studies. Overview of Native American studies, including Indigenous intellectualism and resistance through language revitalization, film-making, and the recognition of one another.

AMST 205.description: Introduction to American Popular Culture. Examines the relation between U.S. national culture, race, and popular culture.

AMST 211.description: Sex in America. Explores how the proliferation of sexual cultures, identities, politics shape everyday lives in the United States and beyond.

AMST 220.description: The Making of Asian America. Historical, social, and cultural analysis of (East, South, and Southeast) Asians in the United States. Theme examined: immigration, race and gender relations, ethnic culture, community, and identity.

AMST 250.description: The African Diaspora. History, political-economy and aesthetics of the African Diaspora with emphasis on Latin America, the Caribbean, Europe and Africa.

AMST 301.description: America, the Frontier, and the New West. Introduction to an interdisciplinary study of American political, cultural and social life with a particular emphasis on the Western United States as a region. Recommended preparation: HIST 200, ENGL 263

AMST 312.description: Documenting Latinx Los Angeles Food Cultures. Explores Latinx food in Los Angeles through an anthropological lens. Students experience, document and analyze local food knowledge and traditions through active field study.

AMST 325.description: The Middle East in Hollywood. An examination of how Hollywood representations of the Middle East have changed over the last 100 years, focusing on how representations influence perceptions and policies.

AMST 336.description: Re-Viewing Religion in Asian America. Interdisciplinary analysis of the religions traditions, institutions, and experiences of Asians and Pacific Islanders in the U.S.

AMST 340.description: Latina/o LA. Examination of spatial and social patterns of the Latino population in Los Angeles. Emphasis on economic, demographic and cultural processes. Duplicates credit in the former GEOG-340.

AMST 345.description: Law and American Indian Studies. Examines indigenous sovereignties and the historical andcontemporary legal histories and cases which inform them.

AMST 348.description: Race and the Environment. Relationships between environmentalism, environmental problems and racial-ethnic minorities. Rise of environmental justice movement. Assessment of social science methods used to investigate these relationships. Duplicates credit in the former GEOG-350.

AMST 350.description: Junior Seminar in American Studies and Ethnicity: Theories and Methods. Advanced study in interdisciplinary theories and methods for  analyzing race and ethnicity in the United Stes, including a  comparative study of topics such as inequality, gender, and class.

AMST 364.description: African American Art. A survey of the fine arts produced by people of African descent in  the United States from the nation's inception in the late 18th  century until the contemporary moment.

AMST 389.description: Carceral Geographies. Focusing on California, interdisciplinary research teams will  study why there are so many new US prisons. What is their  relationship to shopping malls, gated communities, globalization?

AMST 406.description: Social Media Storytelling for Latinx Audiences. Create native journalistic content for current social media and emerging platforms with an emphasis on engaging content for Latinx audiences and underrepresented communities.

AMST 445.description: African American Anthropology. An examination of anthropological research on race and African American culture, from the 18th century to the present.

AMST 449.description: Asian American Literature. Survey of Asian American literature from the earliest time to the  present; development of prose, poetry, and novel.

AMST 452.description: Race, Gender and Sexuality. Examination of sexual discourses in the United States in the context of slavery, empire, sex work, labor markets, schools and prisons.

AMST 458.description: Race and Ethnicity in Entertainment and the Arts. Examines how race and ethnicity as social categories are shaped by communication media; focuses on how race and ethnicity sustain entertainment and media industries.

AMST 464.description: Latino News Media in the United States. History and growing importance of Latino print and broadcast news media in covering immigration, discrimination, culture, social differences and other aspects of U.S. Latino life.
