ANST 694C.description: Doctoral Capstone Project. Mentored research on an individualized topic of interest leading to the professional doctorate. The project will culminate in a formal written research paper or presentation.

CTAN 102.description: Introduction to the Art of Movement. Theory and practice of animation with a focus on movement, gesture, timing and performance. Open to freshman in Animation and Digital Arts majors only.

CTAN 110.description: Design Fundamentals for Animation I. Developing skills in design, composition, shape language, image-making, and visual thinking to create more sophisticated style frames and imagery for animation practice.

CTAN 200.description: The Rise of Digital Hollywood. An overview of the evolution of computer graphics in modern media.

CTAN 201.description: Intermediate Animation Production. Tools, skills and procedures used in animation production with a focus on professional execution of independent and collaborative productions. Prerequisite: CTAN 102. Open to sophomore animation majors only.

CTAN 202.description: Introduction to 3-D Character Animation. 3-D animation performance utilizing preset rigs and virtual characters. Emphasis on timing, gesture, and performance.

CTAN 336.description: Ideation and Pre-Production. Emphasis on lateral thinking working across boundaries to find underlying principles in terms of ideation: the act of becoming an agent of ideas.

CTAN 401B.description: Senior Project. b: Completion and exhibition of the short animated film to demonstrate understanding and further examination of the possibilities of animation time based graphic media. Open to senior animation majors only.

CTAN 420.description: Concept Design for Animation. Creating characters and environments for animation, live action, and video games.

CTAN 425.description: Studio Careers: Story to Screen. Seminar featuring guest speakers from major animation studios to provide an overview of a feature animation pipeline from development to pre-production, production and post-production.

CTAN 432.description: The World of Visual Effects. Introduction to the expanding field of visual effects; topics include integration for cinematic storytelling and the study of digital productions employing the latest visual effects.

CTAN 436.description: Writing for Animation. Workshop exploring concept and structure of long and short form animated films through practical writing exercises.

CTAN 452.description: Introduction to 3-D Computer Animation. Lecture and laboratory in computer animation: geometric modeling, motion specification, lighting, texture mapping, rendering, compositing, production techniques, systems for computer-synthesized animation using Maya software.

CTAN 454.description: Real-Time Animation. The fundamentals of lighting and rendering in real-time. Creating complex, compelling and dynamic scenes and manipulating them in real-time using Unreal Engine.

CTAN 460.description: Character Design Workshop. The basics of character design for animation: anatomy, poses, facial expressions, silhouettes, and anthropomorphism. Development of a portfolio.

CTAN 462.description: Visual Effects. Survey of contemporary concepts and approaches to production in  the current state of film and video effects work.  Digital and  traditional methodologies will be covered, with a concentration on digital exercises illustrating modern techniques.

CTAN 465.description: Digital Effects Animation. All aspects of digital effects animation, including particles, dynamics, and fluids. Creating water, fire, explosions, and destruction in film.

CTAN 480.description: Advanced Character Animation for Games. Advanced techniques for animating 3-D creature characters in games. An emphasis on unique non-human fantasy characters.

CTAN 495.description: Visual Music. Creating visual music animation in a variety of forms and styles. Exploring the relationship between music, movement, and visual expression. Freshmen and sophomores not eligible.

CTAN 496.description: Directed Studies. Individual research under faculty guidance.

CTAN 497.description: Procedural Animation. Introduction to software packages and practices exploring current animation techniques that leverage simulation systems. Artificial intelligence as a tool for animation.

CTAN 503.description: Storyboarding for Animation. Focus on film grammar, perspective, and layout, staging and acting  as it relates to storyboarding for animation.

CTAN 504.description: Creative Production in Virtual Reality. A creative studio course in producing both a linear cinematic virtual reality short film and associated real-time immersive experience.

CTAN 508.description: Compositing and the Art of Creating Visual Styles. A comprehensive overview of compositing techniques to effectively create film looks in 3D/2D animations and visual effects.

CTAN 509.description: Environment Modeling. Create 3D models for environments for urban and natural settings and props including vehicles, rocks, trees and furniture.

CTAN 510.description: Inside Story: Creative Development for Animation. A creative development workshop for animated pitch storytelling, supported by an introduction to character development and story structure fundamentals.

CTAN 535.description: Fundamentals of 3-D Character Animation. Applying traditional principles to 3-D character animation in Maya, with a focus on character performance and acting.

CTAN 543.description: Fictional World Building in Animation. Constructing a persuasive fictional animated world via narrative  techniques, a fixed premise and a degree of believability  supported by five fundamental visual design elements.

CTAN 547.description: Animation Production I. Production of an animation project from creative concept and design through completion.

CTAN 550.description: Stop Motion Puppet and Set Design. Puppet and set design for stop motion animation while providing guidance on armature rigs that allow the character to be animated effectively.

CTAN 564.description: Motion Capture Fundamentals. Fundamental principles of motion capture technology explored while  working through a structured series of assignments based around  performance, gesture and motion.

CTAN 572.description: 3-D Motion Graphic Design. A creative 3-D motion graphics course focusing on animation technique, design and skills in Cinema 4-D.

CTAN 588.description: Cinematic Storytelling for Animators. Techniques and cinematic language employed in both live action and animation by cinematographers and layout artists to tell visual stories.

CTAN 591.description: Animation Pre-Thesis Seminar. Research, development, and preparation of the concept, script, storyboards and preliminary designs for thesis projects to be executed in CTAN 594abz.

CTAN 593.description: Directed Studies in Animation. Individual exploration in the areas of contemporary technology, animation techniques or experimental film through internships, residencies or directed studies. Open only to Animation and Digital Arts master students.

CTAN 594B.description: Master's Thesis. Credit on acceptance of Thesis. Graded CR/NC.

ANTH 105.description: Culture, Medicine and Politics. Survey of the impact of public institutions, private interests and cultural practices on health and the delivery of health care.

ANTH 123.description: Forms of Folklore. Introduction to folklore as a discipline, including folklore research methods and theory. Core course for the minor in Folklore and Popular Culture.

ANTH 124.description: Archaeology of the Americas. A comparative survey of archaeological cultures, Indigenous systems of belief, the complex histories, and deep relationships to landscapes across the Americas. Critically explores anthropological questions.

ANTH 180.description: Anthropology of Capitalism. Uses anthropological frameworks and ethnographic case studies to explore key themes in contemporary capitalism (labor, commodification, markets, finance, entrepreneurship, resistance, authoritarian capitalism).

ANTH 200.description: The Human Animal. Foundations of the human species. Examination of scientific evidence from Darwinian theory, primate behavior, fossils, and the behavior of modern people. Laboratory. Duplicates credit in former ANTH 200Lg.

ANTH 202.description: Archaeology: Our Human Past. Archaeology as the means of investigating our shared human past, from the origins of humanity to the foundations of current civilization.

ANTH 203.description: Global Media. An anthropological approach to examine social and cultural practices of media production, circulation and consumption, engaging with a variety of multimedia.

ANTH 205.description: Introduction to Global Studies and Cross-cultural Research. The effects of globalization on social life in diverse communities, approaching related issues from an ethnographic perspective. Gateway course for the Global Studies Major.

ANTH 220.description: Anthropology of the Environment. Introduces students to anthropological inquiry into human relationships with the environment and provides foundational training in qualitative research methods to investigate environmental issues.

ANTH 255.description: Culture, Performance and Personal Narrative. Explore personal narratives: Stories people tell about their own lives and experiences as objects of artistic expression and sites for formation of individual and social identity.

ANTH 263.description: Exploring Culture through Film. Concepts of social anthropology, using filmic representations of societies throughout the world. Gateway course for the Anthropology major.

ANTH 270.description: Ethnographic Film Past and Present. A selective survey of ethnographic film from the 1890s to 2020s exploring the practice, theory and contemporary relevance of the genre.

ANTH 274.description: Posthuman Anthropology. Examines how posthumanism is reshaping our understanding of humankind, including the ways in which "vernacular posthumanisms" are increasingly enacted in our everyday lives.

ANTH 314.description: The Nature of Maya Civilization. A seminar forum on Maya culture from the earliest form to thepresent; problems of origins, classic florescence, systemscollapse, conquests, persistance, and transformation today.

ANTH 315.description: Native North Americans. Indigenous peoples of North America: major cultural themes, contemporary issues, language revitalization, native sovereignty, environmental issues, decolonization.

ANTH 325.description: Mixed Methods Research for Global and Cross-Cultural Studies. Project-based research practicum emphasizing qualitative methods for cross-cultural analysis. Collecting and interpreting scholarly, ethnographic and archival materials.

ANTH 326.description: European Folklore and Ethnology. Investigates the folklore of Europe, viewing European cultures and societies through an anthropological lens with a focus on shared, expressive cultural traditions.

ANTH 343.description: Heritage Archaeology. An introduction to the field of heritage studies as it is practiced today, examining archaeological, ethnohistorical and ethnographic theory and methodologies, mixed-methods approaches and research.

ANTH 357.description: Cultures of Genocide, Cultures of Care. The comparative analysis of genocide in different cultures and historical moments as well as different cultural responses to it, including human rights and humanitarianism.

ANTH 371.description: Cross-Cultural Research on Urban Gangs. Youth gang dynamics and their effects on institutions. Comparative analysis of Asian, African, and Mexican American gangs.

ANTH 373.description: Magic, Witchcraft and Healing. Analysis of the practices of witches and witch doctors, priests,  diviners and traditional healers in Western and non-Western  societies, relating their practices to religion and medicine.

ANTH 405.description: Evolutionary Medicine. Evolutionary, cultural, and environmental factors in the emergence and existence of diseases; a Darwinian examination of illness in the human species.

ANTH 406.description: Theory and Method in Human Evolutionary Biology. Historical and theoretical approaches to major issues in the field of human evolutionary biology. Capstone course in which students will undertake an original independent research project.

ANTH 411.description: Thesis Seminar in Ethnographic Analysis. Social analysis of qualitative and ethnographic research data, advanced ethnographic writing and representation. Capstone course for Anthropology Major.

ANTH 465.description: Archaeology and Society. The interaction of archaeology and contemporary societies through political and moral claims; archaeologists' role as stewards and interpreters of ancient cultures and their remains. Capstone course for the Archaeology major.

ANTH 476.description: Ethnographic Film Theory from an Historical Perspective. Technologies and uses of, theoretical frameworks for, and the presentation styles of visual ethnographic materials are examined from an historical perspective.

ANTH 485.description: Global Studies Capstone Seminar. Provides senior Global Studies majors with the practical and theoretical skills needed to complete the required Senior Capstone project in Global Studies.

ANTH 490.description: Directed Research.  Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.

ANTH 505.description: Intersubjectivity: Lived Bodies/Relational Selves. Introduction to philosophical, anthropological and sociological considerations of intersubjectivity and experience; narrative approaches to intersubjectivity and relational self-making focusing, especially on clinical encounters.

ANTH 550.description: Global Black Thought. Examines Black intellectual genealogies across a variety of sites and historical periods, with a thematic emphasis on the traffic of ideas and political forms.

ANTH 563.description: Proposal Writing Seminar. Writing proposals is an essential skill for anthropologists in academia and beyond. Provides familiarity with research grant proposals.

ANTH 570.description: Topics in Ethnographic Media Arts. A hands-on approach to contemporary topics in ethnographic media arts and creative nonfiction cinema.

ANTH 590.description: Directed Research. Research conducted at the master's or pre-PhD candidacy level. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded C/NC.

ANTH 790.description: Research. Research leading to the doctorate. Maximum number of units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

ANTH 794C.description: Doctoral Dissertation. Credit on acceptance of Dissertation. Graded IP/CR/NC.

AAN 500.description: Applied Business Analytics and Artificial Intelligence. Foundational principles and practical applications of analytics and artificial intelligence (AI) across various business domains with a focus on challenges involved in these techniques.

AAN 505.description: Statistics for Applied Data Analytics. Statistics, probability, probability distributions and other fundamental data analysis concepts and tools. Development of simple models to support subsequent evaluation and data-supported decisions.

AAN 510.description: Visualization and Storytelling With Data. Tools and techniques to effectively analyze and visualize data and communicate the results. Python libraries, modules, techniques and best practices.

AAN 515.description: Regression Modeling for Applied Predictive Analytics. Linear regression and logistic regression models, coefficient interpretation and performance analysis. Advanced modeling techniques.

AAN 520.description: Applied Data Management and Database Systems. Overview of the data pipeline, data sources, data interchange formats and the organization of data for analytics and modeling, problems, solutions and best practices.

AAN 525.description: Applied Machine Learning for Business Applications. Exploration of machine learning principles and practices using real-world data, models and techniques. Initial data explorations to deployment to maintenance of machine learning systems.

AAN 530.description: Applied Optimization and Simulation. Applied mathematical programming including simulation methods, constrained optimization methods, linear programming, mixed integer programming and statistical and discrete event simulation methods. Case studies.

AAN 535.description: Analytics Business Strategy and Communication. Development of astute business acumen and strong communication skills for analytics professionals and leaders in relation to strategy, storytelling, communication and change management.

AAN 540.description: Applications of Deep Learning and AI in Business. Exploration of deep learning models, deep neural networks and artificial intelligence sequence modeling and implementation. Applications of targeted techniques to real-world business scenarios.

AAN 550.description: Applications in Artificial Intelligence. A comprehensive survey of generative artificial intelligence and artificial intelligence for decision-making; transformer and diffusion models; reinforcement learning and causal inference. Hands-on implementation.

AAN 555.description: Applied Analytics and Artificial Intelligence Capstone. An integrative culminating experience of the MSAAN program. The practical application of knowledge and skills gained throughout the program to address a significant business problem.

ARAB 122.description: Arabic I. Introduction to Modern Standard Arabic: Development of speaking, listening, reading, and writing skills in contemporary cultural contexts. (Duplicates credit in former MDES 122)

ARAB 152.description: Arabic II. Continuation of Arabic I. Prerequisite: ARAB-122. (Duplicates credit in former MDES 152)

ARAB 222.description: Arabic III. Intermediate Modern Standard Arabic. Continued development of speaking, listening, reading, and writing skills. Prerequisite: ARAB 152. (Duplicates credit in former MDES 222)

ARCG 298A.description: Introduction to Scientific Diving. Extensive academic preparation in the physics, physiology, safety, and methodology for in-water scientific diving.

ARCG 298B.description: Introduction to Scientific Diving. Extensive academic preparation in the physics, physiology, safety, and methodology for in-water scientific diving.

ARCG 308.description: Techniques and Issues in 3D Imaging and Modeling. In-depth exploration of applications, techniques and standards involved in stereoscopic imaging and photogrammetric modeling.

ARCG 322.description: Roman Art and Archaeology. Survey of the art and architecture of ancient Rome and its empire, from the beginnings of the city through Constantine (8th century BCE to 4th century CE).

ARCG 370.description: Digs and Dispute: Religion and Archaeology in Israel. Investigates contemporary conflicts in the discovery of the ancient world. Students will ask essential questions about the power of discovering and showcasing specific narratives.

ARCG 403.description: Dare to Care for the Past. Experiential academic learning opportunities in the archaeology laboratory, collections, or other facilities for archaeology, heritage, or material culture studies skill-building, research, and professional development.

ARCG 490.description: Directed Research. Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.

ARCH 102B.description: Architectural Design I.  Introduction to principles and processes; sequence of exercises emphasizing development of basic skills, ideas, and techniques used in the design of simplified architectural projects.

ARCH 105B.description: Fundamentals of Design Communication. Visual communication techniques applicable to the design of the built environment; drawing, photography, modeling.

ARCH 106.description: Workshop in Architecture. Introduction to the ways architecture is created and understood, for minors and non-majors. Hands-on discussion and laboratory session with some drawing and model building. Not available for credit to architecture majors.

ARCH 108.description: Idea to Reality. Examines the entrepreneurial process of taking a product from idea to marketplace, including innovation, concepts of feasibility, design, prototyping, getting investors and marketing.

ARCH 109.description: Design Foundation Workshop. Introduction to concepts and principles that are the distinguishing attributes of the architectural discourse and to the range of skills essential to the design process.

ARCH 202B.description: Architectural Design II.  Continuing development of principles and processes: sequence of projects selected to broaden awareness of design issues at various scales in the urban context. Prerequisite: 102abL.

ARCH 205B.description: Building Science I.  The process and communication of building design: physical building shell, systems for structure, enclosure, and space ordering.

ARCH 211.description: Materials and Methods of Building Construction. Basic considerations and design implications of the problem of determination of the materials and the construction details and processes for buildings.

ARCH 213B.description: Building Structures and Seismic Design. Investigation and design of structure systems : their resistance toseismic and wind forces and integration with architectural design for synergy of form and structure.

ARCH 214B.description: World History of Architecture. A world-wide perspective of architectural history as a product of social, cultural, religious and political dimensions, 1500 CE to present.

ARCH 220.description: The Architect's Sketchbook. The architect's sketchbook as a portable laboratory for perceivingand documenting space introduces the study of the builtenvironment. On-site sessions develop drawing, observation, and visualization skills.

ARCH 228.description: Social Environments. Exploration of the intersection between the urban form and the social life of cities, looking at systemic problems of urban societies and potential design solutions.

ARCH 229.description: Shelter Design Workshop. Introduction to design at an occupiable scale -- from tents and pavilions to single units of housing, including issues of materiality, accessibility, constructability, functionality, etc.

ARCH 302B.description: Architectural Design III. Special integrative year including design issues relating to  housing.

ARCH 303.description: Principles of Spatial Design I. Introduction to design principles and processes; sequence of exercises emphasizing development of basic skills, ideas, and techniques used in the creation of simplified urban space design projects.

ARCH 305B.description: Building Science II.  The design of a building as a complex of interacting systems;     relations of subsystems; influences of production and marketing on design.

ARCH 315.description: Design for the Luminous and Sonic Environment.  Ideas, problems, and computations related to the design of buildings in response to the luminous and sonic environment.

ARCH 316.description: Place and Culture. (Study abroad programs only)  Study of the relationships between places and culture through readings, lectures, discussion and  weekly field trips.

ARCH 328.description: Entrepreneurial Practices for Architecture. Development of business acumen around new architectural products, materials, systems, etc. Marketing, pitching, business plan development and networking are important aspects of business that all early entrepreneurs need to learn and understand.

ARCH 329.description: Professional Practicum Workshop. Students are required to have an architecture-related internship. Students reflect on the nature of their internships and the practice in general through readings and assignments.

ARCH 402B.description: Architectural Design IV. Selected areas of specialization; three projects chosen with  advisement from a variety of studio offerings that concentrate on  different areas of vital concern.

ARCH 404.description: Topics in Modern Architecture in Southern California. Investigation of modern architecture in Southern California within  its cultural and historic contexts.

ARCH 405B.description: Building Science III.  Design of building systems as an experimental process. Prereq: ARCH 305abL.

ARCH 406.description: Global Studies: Topics in                        Architecture, Urbanism, History and Art         . Offered for particular geographic areas of study. Required prerequisite for all full semester undergraduate global programs. Also intended for general interest in focused study on particular geographic area.

ARCH 411.description: Architectural Technology. Architectural design considered as a technological problem; influence of technology on design; buildings as integrated sets of subsystems.

ARCH 412.description: Geodesign Practicum. Application of design concepts, planning protocols and spatial analysis skills to a complex planning or design problem sponsored by a local public, private or not-for-profit client in a studio setting.

ARCH 414.description: Perspectives in History and Theory in Architecture. Perspectives in Architecture and Urbanism is an advanced course that allows students to delve deeply into one aspect of world history, theory and/or contemporary issues to develop more focused and critical understanding of that discourse.

ARCH 421.description: Digital Architectural Photography. Perceiving and documenting the built environment through the  perspective and frame of the digital camera. Mastering the basic  principles of the digital image through an understanding of frame,  light, exposure, color correction and printing output.

ARCH 424.description: Field Studies in Architecture. Field studies using direct observation, site  recordings/documentation, analysis and evaluation supplemented by  discussions and readings in architecture.  Departmental approval.  Recommended preparation: core curriculum

ARCH 425.description: Field Studies in Urbanism. Field studies using direct observation, site  recordings/documentation, analysis and evaluation supplemented by  discussions and readings in urbanism.  Departmental approval.  Recommended preparation: core curriculum

ARCH 426.description: Field Studies in Tectonics. Field studies using direct observation, site  recordings/documentation, analysis and evaluation supplemented by  discussions and readings in tectonics.  Departmental approval.  Recommended preparation: core curriculum

ARCH 431.description: Nonconventional Materials for the Built Environment. An exploration of materials science topics relevant to the application of nonconventional materials in architecture, design, and engineering, addressing a broad range of materials, from the experimental to the vernacular.

ARCH 469.description: Mixed Use Development Process. Design, financial, legal and management challenges of mixed use real estate development; field project.

ARCH 470B.description: Architectural Studies Capstone. Collaborative research project and research paper in an area of concentration.

ARCH 480.description: Conversations on the Expanded Role of the Architect. Modeled after Renaissance Salons, this "flipped classroom" course relies on lectures by luminaries and discussions as a means to interrogate the role of the architect.

ARCH 499.description: Special Topics.  Selected topics in various specialty areas of architecture.

ARCH 502A.description: Architectural Design V. The final architectural project under the guidance of a faculty adviser to demonstrate architectural knowledge, skills, and professional interests and goals.

ARCH 505B.description: Graduate Architecture Design I. A general introduction to architectural principles, intended to develop design and critical thinking skills and proficiency to communicate those ideas effectively. Open to graduate architecture majors only.

ARCH 507.description: Theories of Computer Technology. Fundamental theories and meanings of computation as a technique in architectural design.

ARCH 514B.description: Global History of Architecture . A historical survey of global architecture, analyzed as a product of social, cultural, religious and political forces.a: 4500 BCE to 1500 CE; b: 1500 CE to present.

ARCH 517.description: Current Topics in Building Science. Critical studies in building science ranging from sustainability, lighting, acoustics, materials and methods, structures, energy issues, digital media, and fabrication. Students focus on minimum of two topics.

ARCH 519.description: Sustainability in the Environment:               Infrastructures, Urban Landscapes, and Buildings. Methodologies and exercises on contextual design and  environmentally sound technologies (EST's) applications for the  sustainability of urban infrastructures, operative landscapes, and  building integration in the urban system.

ARCH 523A.description: Structural Design and Analysis. a. Introduction to behavior and analysis of building structures. Structural loading, materials, and element types will be explored to understand the basic building blocks of buildings. b. Investigation and design of building structural systems for gravity, wind and seismic loading. Comprehensive design exploration of framing type, materials, detailing, layout, form and integration. Recommended preparation: One-semester college-level course in physics or calculus.

ARCH 525.description: Professional Practice: Pre-Design, Project and   Office Administration                           . Design methodology, typology programming, site analysis, budget formulation and pro-forma procedures. Office management, emphasizing professional service and professional ethics as well as project management focusing on the architect's responsibilities during construction.

ARCH 526.description: Professional Practice: Legal and Economic        Context, Project Documentation                  . The laws and regulations that affect architecture as well as building economics and financing.   Development of comprehensive project documentation, detailing, specifications, drawing formats and organizations.

ARCH 527.description: Case Studies: The Development of Urban Housing. An exploration of the various elements and stages of the housing  development process.  Recommended preparation: a preliminary  understanding of real estate or housing.

ARCH 529.description: Urban Housing: Programs, Precedents, and Recent Case Studies. Historical overview of the major domestic and international housing developments and innovations since the early 20th century case study format examining a wide range of issues that determine the form of urban housing in various cultures. Major emphasis on the detail analysis of social, technical, and design factors affecting recent housing developments. Recommended preparation: two years of undergraduate architectural studies.

ARCH 534.description: Landscape Construction: Topographic Design. Techniques, strategies, materials, and standards to topographic design and construction in landscape architecture. In-class labs practice basic grading, drainage design, and stormwater management.

ARCH 535.description: Landscape Construction: Performance Approaches. Develop tools and knowledge to expand the performative boundaries of landscape architecture beyond common typologies. Topics range from ecological infrastructure to design with weather patterns. A systematic approach to case studies, landscape technologies, and field trips seeds the knowledge base and representational methods necessary to design and build these complex landscape performances.

ARCH 537.description: Plant Ecology + Identification. Principles and concepts of plant ecology and regional plant identification; introduction to California native plant species and communities with field trips and case studies.

ARCH 541B.description: Landscape Architecture Design. Projects in urban settings with emphasis on landscape continuities  as well as development of integrative schematic proposals and  detailed open space design.

ARCH 542B.description: Landscape Architecture Design. Projects for the public realm with emphasis on urbanity and  connectivity, place and meaning.

ARCH 544.description: Landscape as Urbanism: Case Studies. Cities predominantly in the Global South are studied in relationship to landscape systems. Focus on historic and future urbanization at the interface of natural systems and climate dynamics.

ARCH 545.description: Contemporary Theories of Landscape Architecture. Explores contemporary landscape architecture theories, propositions and projects in the context of cities. The exploration methodology includes the study of epochal projects and theoretical texts.

ARCH 547.description: Advanced Topics in Urban Ecology. Builds on knowledge related to the impacts of anthropocentrism on our current environmental/landscape condition - stresses on biodiversity, urban heat island, sea-level rise, etc, and strategies at mitigating these conditions - urban forestry, building soils, etc.

ARCH 548.description: Media for Landscape Architecture: 3D Design. Developing and communicating landscape architecture design intent using visualization tools for three-dimensional studies.

ARCH 549.description: Fundamentals of Heritage Conservation. Concepts and strategies for conservation of significant elements of the built environment: buildings, sites and communities as revealed by readings, site visits, and case studies.

ARCH 550.description: Heritage Conservation Policy and Planning. Conservation practice within an economic, political, and cultural context looking at the regulatory environment, public advocacy and policy, real estate development, heritage tourism, environmental sustainability, cultural diversity, and interpretation. Recommended Preparation: ARCH-549.

ARCH 551.description: Conservation Methods and Materials. Concepts and techniques for building conservation including identification of treatments, recordation and research, material properties and behavior, building forensics, and project implementation. Recommended preparation: ARCH-549.

ARCH 554.description: Heritage Conservation Practicum  Advanced Documentation. Heritage conservation practicum utilizing in-depth documentation methodology to explore the historic built environment of greater Los Angeles. Topics will vary from year to year; may be repeated for credit when subject matter is different.

ARCH 555.description: Global Perspectives in Heritage Conservation. In-depth analysis of international heritage conservation practice with a focus on a single country, continent, or world region outside the United States. Topics will vary from year to year; may be repeated for credit when subject matter is different.

ARCH 557.description: Sustainable Conservation of the Historic Built Environment. Analysis of the intersection between green building and historic resources with an emphasis on stewardship and sustainability.

ARCH 560.description: A History of Architectural Theory: 1400-1914. A seminar on architectural history from Alberti to Scott, reviewing primary texts and subsequent criticisms.

ARCH 561.description: Urbanism Themes and Case Studies. Examines urbanism through case studies in theory and design to understand the impacts of globalization, technology, and sustainability on the contemporary city.

ARCH 563.description: Contemporary Architectural Theory. Investigates, compares, and critiques modern and contemporary theories of the designed and built environment by focusing on key figures, movements, and texts.

ARCH 573.description: Seismic Design. Theory, design methodology and practice of how seismicity affects architecture and structural system selection required for robust earthquake performance and seismic sustainability.

ARCH 574.description: Parametric Design. An in depth and critical look into the reasons and uses for parametric design and its relationship to contemporary form, fabrication, and construction of the built environment.

ARCH 575B.description: Systems. The fundamental scientific principles governing light and sound in the built environment will be examined in the context of human physiological, psychological and biological needs.

ARCH 576.description: Sustainable Design for Healthy Indoor Environments . Course outlines the building design and its performance diagnostic processes required to assure indoor environmental quality and the building occupants environmental health, productivity, and physiological comfort.

ARCH 577.description: Lighting Design. The physics, technical knowledge, professional knowledge, design, and documentation processes used in architectural lighting design, including first principles, manual calculations and computer simulations..

ARCH 578.description: Engineering Design: Industrialized and Modular Construction. Integration of architecture, engineering and construction practices through the development of a construction project.

ARCH 581.description: Techniques in Digital Fabrication. A practical introduction to digital fabrication. Covered topics include 3D surface milling, thermoforming, materials, casting and shop technology as applied to repeatable surfaces in architecture.

ARCH 585.description: Visual Storytelling and Entrepreneurship in Media. Investigating visual stories as an active tool to critically explore and express design ideas; positions social media and crowdfunding as a foundation for creative action. Not open to Freshmen and Sophomores.

ARCH 587.description: Light the Night...or Not?. Explores principles and applications of exterior lighting design through lectures, demonstrations and experiments. Emphasizes perception, impact, integration of light with architectural forms and the environment.

ARCH 605B.description: Graduate Architecture Design- Comprehensive. b. Comprehensive project emphasizing the interaction between general principles and local sites, building technologies and total building design. Open only to Architecture majors.

ARCH 606.description: Advanced Architectural Theory. Interrogates the architectural and cultural landscape of our contemporary cities through a combination of lectures and seminars on theories of place, identity, aesthetics, and technology.

ARCH 607.description: Advanced Computation. Introduction to a range of new technologies and techniques examining their technical and theoretical implications including advanced computational design techniques and geospatial design tools.

ARCH 608.description: Urban Theory: Los Angeles Case Study. Critically investigates the urban condition of Los Angeles through lectures, readings, and field visits. Aims to heighten awareness of the entwinement of environment, culture, architecture and the contemporary city.

ARCH 609.description: Advanced Digital Fabrication. Introduction to a range of new technologies and techniques examining technical and theoretical implications including a range of digital fabrication technologies, robotics and film-making techniques.

ARCH 611.description: Advanced Building Systems Integration. Design criteria development, material and construction process  methods, occupancy based load profiles, performance/material  life-cycle-mandates, durability for advanced building systems  including integrity in sustainable urban systems.

ARCH 615.description: Seminar: Environmental Systems Research.  A detailed examination of current issues in the thermal,          acoustical and radiant environment; recent developments in         criteria, systems, controls, design tools and simulations; an      understanding of the relationships between environmental factors,  economics, and architectural goals.

ARCH 672.description: Future Building Skins: Advanced Applications in Architecture. Focuses on the development of novel facade solutions that respond to shortcomings of contemporary facades applications in both new and existing buildings.

ARCH 691A.description: Heritage Conservation Thesis Preparation and Thesis. Introduction to, and exploration of, topics leading to the development of a thesis prospectus and directed research towards the completion of the master's thesis in heritage conservation.

ARCH 691B.description: Heritage Conservation Thesis Preparation and Thesis. Introduction to, and exploration of, topics leading to the development of a thesis prospectus and directed research towards the completion of the master's thesis in heritage conservation.

ARCH 692B.description: Building Science Thesis. Research and thesis for the Master of Building Science degree.

ARCH 694.description: Research Publication Methods for Building Science. Technical documentation, graphic representation, and verbal presentation for writing and presenting journal articles and conference presentations in building science.

ARCH 698B.description: Advanced Design-Research. Directed research option for the MLArch degree.

ARCH 790.description: Doctoral Research. Research leading to the doctorate.  Maximum units which may be  applied to the degree to be determined by the School of  Architecture.  Graded CR/NC.

ARCH 793B.description: Architecture Directed Design Research Option I. Directed Design Research option for graduate level architecture degree. Credit on acceptance of research project. Open only to Architecture majors. Graded IP/CR/NC.

ART 105.description: Art and Design Studio I. Introduction to the fundamental elements in art making, design creation and thinking, including key principles of  process and critical analysis.

ART 106.description: Art and Design Studio II. Introduction to the fundamental elements in art making, design creation and thinking, including the key principles of process and critical analysis.

ART 110.description: Drawing for Art and Design. An introduction to drawing, both skill and perception oriented, as the basic tool for all the visual arts and design.

ART 120.description: Painting I. Practical introduction to oil and acrylic pigments, painting tools, mediums, processes and contemporary concepts. Primary experience in: color, composition and perception through representational and abstract painting.

ART 130.description: Ceramics I. Practical and theoretical exploration of the nature of surface, form, volume and mass as fundamental elements of clay sculpture and the ceramic object.

ART 131.description: Wheel Throwing. An introductory course using wheel throwing techniques for ceramics to explore a variety of forms through three-dimensional exercises.

ART 140.description: Sculpture I. Practical and theoretical introduction to sculpture as dimensional manipulation. Primary exploration of form, mass, gravity, surface, structure and associative recognition in three-dimensional art.

ART 141.description: Creating and Understanding Visuals. Lecture-studio course on the theory and history behind contemporary art, design, and visual communication; students also create work, informed by ideas from the lecture.

ART 149.description: Black and White Film and Darkroom Photography. Introduces film cameras, development, and darkroom techniques, photographic history, theory and practice within an art context.

ART 150.description: Introduction to Photography: Process and Concept. Digital photography as a medium of contemporary art. Includes  concept development, DSLR cameras, lighting, digital workflow,  software, large format printing and installation.

ART 205.description: Foundation Studio Intensive. Cohort building studio intensive that ensures incoming transfers have foundational concepts and skill sets for intermediate and advanced studio courses.

ART 207A.description: Two-Dimensional Art Workshop. Studio practice to develop drawing fundamentals for game designers, animators and narrative artists.

ART 207B.description: Two-Dimensional Art Workshop. Continuation of ART 207a.

ART 260.description: Introduction to Video: Projection and Virtual Worlds in Art. An introductory course exploring contemporary processes and practices of video experimentation in art including the camera, editing, digital manipulation and spatial and virtual platforms.

ART 280.description: Studio Critique I. Interdisciplinary forum where students develop research skills, learn how to best articulate their artistic production, discuss materials related to their research interests, and critique the work of their peers.

ART 310.description: Drawing II. Directed examination of personal approaches to drawing with emphasis on making visual and artistic decisions and developing additional skills and sources of inspiration. Individual expression will be encouraged.

ART 312.description: Comics Project. All aspects of comics will be covered, from writing and composition to inking and marketing through the production of an individual multi-page comic creation.

ART 314.description: Illustration for Art and Design. Illustration techniques and professional practices across the range of fine art, comics, editorial illustration, narrative arts, visual development and others. Digital and hybrid approaches.

ART 330.description: Ceramics II. Directed examination of aesthetic concepts and investigation into personal ideas as they relate to the development of a creative visual language in ceramics.

ART 340.description: Sculpture II. Directed examination of three-dimensional aesthetic concepts; development of an individual creative vision.

ART 362.description: Ideas in Intermedia. An examination of the impact of digital media on contemporary culture, with attention to a particular, changing topic each semester.

ART 370.description: Printmaking. Introductory course in various printmaking techniques; necessary skills and inherent expressive qualities of different printmaking methods are explored.

ART 380.description: Studio Critique II. A continuation of ART 280 for third-year students, providing an interdisciplinary forum for artistic practice and a deepening critique of one's work and the work of peers.

ART 412.description: Advanced Comics Project. Creation of an advanced comic/chapter of a graphic novel of meaningful content, development of the student voice and to learn professional practices for careers in Comics.

ART 415.description: Studies in Drawing and Painting. A studio examination of rotating topics in drawing/painting, either media-based or content-driven, with individual and collaborative projects; topics change each semester.

ART 417.description: Digital Painting Studio. Create a portfolio of images reflecting student interests, voice and sensibilities, through digital painting/drawing and using the software and hardware of their choice.

ART 418.description: Independent Studies in Studio Arts. Independent research of specific topics under the direction of a faculty member. Administrative and faculty approval required.

ART 419.description: Professional Internship in the Arts. An experiential/academic opportunity in a museum, gallery, community cultural center or related facility. Lectures, seminars, written analysis and working internship.

ART 420.description: Topics in Advanced Painting. Examination of personal approaches and professional careers in painting and 2D art making, emphasis on making a body of  work with creative freedom in committed studio space.

ART 430.description: Topics in Advanced Ceramics. Continued directed examination of aesthetic concepts and investigation into personal ideas as they relate to the development of a creative visual language in ceramics.

ART 443.description: Woodworking. Exploration of the essential skills in woodworking through lecture, demonstration and hands-on training. Includes instruction in joinery and relevant machinery and hand tools.

ART 444.description: Modeling and Mold Making. Introduction to plaster mold making using clay and wax for both ceramics and sculpture. Exploration of various casting materials.

ART 445.description: Metal. Introduction to metal in fine art. Emphasis on technical proficiencies and effective solutions working in a variety of metals.

ART 450.description: Topics in Advanced Photography. In-depth exploration of photographic and artistic concepts as they apply to the articulation of personal work.

ART 452.description: Cut and Paste: Photo Collage Analog and Digital. Exploration of methods with working photographically through collage.

ART 461.description: Motion Graphics for Art and Video. An intensive investigation of the mechanics and methodology of contemporary software for video art. Recommended to be taken concurrently with ART 260.

ART 470.description: Topics in Advanced Printmaking. Directed examination of specific printmaking media in relation to personal aesthetic goals and expressive concepts.

ART 484.description: Contemporary Issues in Art. An advanced studio and discussion course aims to expand a students relationship to, and understanding of, contemporary artistic dissemination, discourse, and display via a series of rotating topics.

ART 485.description: Studio Capstone. A faculty-mentored course supporting advanced conceptual exploration and the development of an ambitious, self-defined series or body of work; may culminate in a group exhibition or individual project.

ART 494A.description: Senior Thesis. Individual research under guidance of faculty member for senior-level BFA students, leading to a substantial paper or other project.

ART 515.description: Visiting Artist and Scholar Seminar. Lecture and discussion course in the professional practice of art featuring formal presentations by visiting artists and scholars. (Duplicates credit in FA 515)

ART 520.description: Individual Studies. Investigation of creative problems through various media. Course may be repeated. (Duplicates credit in former FA 520)

lectures.instructor: Edgar Arceneaux; China Adams; Patty Chang
Edgar Arceneaux; China Adams; Patty Chang

ART 525.description: Making and Curating Art: Pedagogy and Praxis. Provides students with a foundation in the history and theory of studio art and curatorial education and develops their teaching skills in these areas.

ART 535.description: Group Critique. Presentation and critique which builds students' skills in presenting and contextualizing their artwork for peer review; analytic discussion regarding directions in contemporary art.

ART 590.description: Directed Research. Research leading to graduate degree. Maximum units which may be applied to degree determined by department. Graded CR/NC. (Duplicates credit in former FA 590)

ART 594A.description: Master's Thesis. Credit on acceptance of Thesis. Open only to master students. Graded CR/NC. (Duplicates credit in former FA 594a)

ART 594B.description: Master's Thesis. Credit on acceptance of Thesis. Open only to master students. Graded CR/NC. (Duplicates credit in former FA 594b)

ART 594Z.description: Master's Thesis. Credit on acceptance of Thesis. Open only to master students. Graded CR/NC. (Duplicates credit in former FA 594z)

AHIS 121.description: Foundations of Western Art: Renaissance to Contemporary. European art and its legacy in the Americas. Painting, sculpture, architecture and other visual media considered in relation to social and cultural history.

AHIS 125.description: Arts of Asia: Antiquity to 1300. An introduction to the major art forms and monuments of religious art in India, Southeast Asia, China and Japan from prehistory to1300.

AHIS 215.description: Studies in Architecture and Urbanism. Analyzing a wide range of case studies, this course provides a roadmap to analyze and interpret the built environment in many different eras and contexts.

AHIS 238.description: The Russian Monarchy: Representation, Power, and Autocracy                                       . Examines the Russian monarchy and its representation in history    and the arts. It studies film, literature, painting, sculpture,    historiography, and political ideologies.

AHIS 250.description: Art, Modernity and Difference. Consideration of various categories of "The Modern" as they have been constructed in Western art of the late 19th and 20th centuries.

AHIS 301.description: Guardians of the Past?:Art Preservation, Ethics, and the Law. Introduction to key ethical, historical, and legal debates about art preservation and collecting across the globe.

AHIS 368.description: Modern Art I: 1700-1850. A cultural and historical examination of European art and  architecture from 1700 (Rococo) to 1850 (Realism), focusing on the  beginnings of modernism in the age of revolution.

AHIS 370.description: Modern Art III: 1940 to the Present. Questions of social engagement and political structure address this examination of major international movements in art since 1940.

AHIS 385.description: Later Chinese Art. A survey of Chinese painting from 900 to the present, emphasizing the role of painting within the context of Chinese intellectual history.

AHIS 400.description: Undergraduate Apprenticeship. Independent work in art museums, galleries or art history related  institutes supervised by on-site professionals and USC faculty.    Not available for credit for AHIS majors. CR/NC

AHIS 427.description: Archaeological Theories, Methods, and Practice. Various theoretical approaches, methods, and practice of archaeology in a seminar style format, with lectures, oral presentations, and museum visits.

AHIS 449.description: History of Prints and Drawings.  Aspects of the history of the graphic arts; stylistic and technical considerations may both be included or specific areas stressed at the choice of the instructor.

AHIS 470.description: Studies in Contemporary Art. In-depth exploration of specified topics within the area of contemporary art and architecture.

AHIS 483.description: East Asian Garden and Designed Landscape. Explores the transmigration of Japanese art and aesthetics and the politics of their adaptation and assimilation in Los Angeles.

AHIS 485.description: Material Culture of the Silk Road. Introduction to the history and material culture of the Silk Road with emphasis on the arts of Dunhuang and Kucha.

AHIS 490.description: Directed Research.  Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.

AHIS 494.description: Undergraduate Proseminar in Art History. Historiography and methodology: introduction to techniques of research and writing. Required of all art history majors, preferably in junior year.

AHIS 495A.description: Undergraduate Honors Thesis. Research and writing of original thesis under guidance of faculty member. Prereq: Consent of instructor.

AHIS 495B.description: Undergraduate Honors Thesis. Research and writing of original thesis under guidance of faculty member. Prereq: Consent of instructor.

AHIS 500.description: Methods and Theory of Art History. Methodologies, theories and critical traditions that have shaped the discipline. Emphasis will vary depending on faculty. Required of all first-year M.A. and Ph.D. candidates. Open to graduate or limited status students in art history only.

AHIS 590.description: Directed Research.  Research leading to graduate degree. Maximum units which may be applied to degree determined by department.  Graded CR/NC.

AHIS 790.description: Research. Research leading to the Doctorate. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department.

AHIS 794B.description: Doctoral Dissertation. Credit on acceptance of Dissertation. Graded CR/NC.

ARTL 502.description: Issues in the Arts and the Contemporary World. Examination of major environmental trends including changing demographics, new business models, rapidly developing technology and globalization, and understanding their implications for the arts.

ARTL 504.description: Arts and the Community: Current Practice and New Visions                                         . Exploration of a range of ideas, ideologies and strategies that have historically been used to connect arts organizations to their communities.

ARTL 510.description: Arts Leadership Practicum. Year-long practicum which puts ideas and concepts into practice. Each student will conceptualize, develop, and complete an arts project of his/her own choosing.

ARTL 590.description: Directed Research.  Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which maybe applied to the degree to be determined by the department.Graded CR/NC.

ARTL 598.description: Internship for Arts Leadership. Practical work experience in the student's field of study, at an off-campus location. Students are individually supervised by faculty.

ARTL 790.description: Research.  Research leading to the doctorate. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

ACAD 174.description: Innovators Forum. Leaders in diverse disciplines, industries and the arts present and discuss problems facing society and critique real-world projects that challenge the concept of innovation.

ACAD 176.description: Rapid Visualization. Techniques, methods, concepts, tools, and materials that are used to quickly visualize and communicate ideas and develop problem-solving skills.

ACAD 177.description: Digital Toolbox: Design. Basics of industry-standard creative, analytical and presentation software. Applications include design, illustration, presentation and publishing.

ACAD 178.description: Digital Toolbox: Motion Graphics. Basics of industry standard software for motion graphics, visual effects, animation design, generative art and interactive visual experiences.

ACAD 181.description: Disruptive Innovation. Critical approaches to social and cultural changes stemming from disruptive innovations in the arts, science, technology, communications, new media, politics and business. Open only to Arts, Technology and the Business of Innovation students.

ACAD 184.description: Operations Management and Finance for Challenge-Based Innova. Operations management and financial literacy emphasizing capacity planning, supply chains, financial modeling and decision-making to optimize efficiency, sustainability and organizational growth in dynamic environments.

ACAD 186.description: Digital Toolbox: Computational Visual Design. The use of algorithms in custom-designed computer software for visual output; applications in the areas of graphic design, interaction design, motion graphics and simulation.

ACAD 188.description: Modeling Products with Solidworks. Tools and techniques for Solidworks CAD design and design improvements, specially focused on the ideation and development of new products.

ACAD 206.description: Communication and Culture. Examines cultural institutions, ideologies, artifacts, and productions; role of culture in everyday life; cultural studies as methodology; culture and power.

ACAD 207.description: Narrative Technology and the Human Experience. Exploring craft and innovation in communicating concepts, products  and experiences. Students employ video narration, interaction and  augmented reality in service of engaging an audience.

ACAD 222.description: Introduction to Machine Intelligence. Introduction to artificial intelligence and machine learning through programming models, training models with several methodologies, support vector machines, decision trees, ensemble learning and random forests.

ACAD 230.description: Introduction to Interactive Physical Computing. Design and development of physical computing prototypes within the intersection of electronics, computing, design, consumer electronics and product design.

ACAD 245.description: Fundamentals of Product Design. Introductory course in learning how to design physical products, including the processes for determining consumer need, market opportunity and competitive product analysis.

ACAD 260.description: Introduction to Healthcare Innovation. Introductions to various health innovations, including pathways, technology, techniques and outcomes. A framework for innovation in healthcare and overview of tools for health innovators.

ACAD 274.description: Designing Interactive Data Systems. The design of interactive interfaces for data systems and simulations; introduction to business intelligence, data engineering, web development and user experience design.

ACAD 280.description: Information Design. Designing elegant and powerful graphic user interfaces for interacting with visual displays of quantitative information.

ACAD 281.description: Constructing Experiences. Experience-based solutions for the design of digital and physical environments, and the development of entertaining, informational and inspirational interactions based on human behavior.

ACAD 288.description: Constructing Digital Worlds. The design and construction of digital twins for objects and environments with real-time rendering and collaboration; workflow optimization; 3D data aggregation.

ACAD 307.description: Punk, Counterculture, and the Do-It-Yourself (DIY) Ethos. Explores punk, hip hop, and DIY countercultures as transformative  forces in social activism, media innovation, creative  entrepreneurship, and equitable, alternative cultural and artistic  practices.

ACAD 308.description: Computer-Aided Design for Bio-Mechanical Systems. Concepts of computer-aided design in 2-dimensions and 3-dimensions. Creating advanced parts using extrusions, surfaces, and equation driven sketches. Forming assemblies and sub-assemblies, for motion analysis

ACAD 309.description: Dreams and Madness: The Art of Japan's Golden Age of Animation. An in-depth look at the art, politics, and cultural impact of  several Japanese filmmakers including Isao Takahata, Hayao  Miyazaki, Satoshi Kon, Mamoru Hosoda and Makoto Shinkai.

ACAD 311.description: Design for User Experience. Fundamental concepts, techniques, practices, workflows and tools associated with the practice of user experience and interaction design in web and mobile applications.

ACAD 312.description: Materials Behavior and Processing. Mechanical behavior of metals, polymers, ceramics, and composites. Structure-process-property relationships. Mechanical testing, stress-strain relationships, microstructural characteristics and analysis. Material failure (fracture, fatigue, creep) and degradation.

ACAD 315.description: Basics of Project and Operations Management for Non-Majors. Introduction to tools and methods for the design, production, and delivery of goods and services. Techniques for planning, monitoring, and controlling complex projects. Not available for degree or major credit for business and accounting majors. Duplicates credit in BUAD 311 and BUAD 313.

ACAD 324.description: The Practice of Design: Ideation to Innovation. History and application of proven collaborative design processes and methodologies as they relate to ideation and innovation.

ACAD 325.description: Human Technology Interaction and the User Experience. The user experience lifecycle from ideation to prototype evaluation with a focus on principles, processes and practices essential for designing effective digital products and experiences.

ACAD 342.description: iOS App Development. Introduction to the Swift programming language, various frameworks, and design patterns needed to develop applications for iOS mobile devices such as iPhones and iPads.

ACAD 360.description: Design Strategy: Problem Solving for Organizations. A professional, collaborative and multidisciplinary consulting approach to diagnosing problems and applying design-based solutions on behalf of organizations.

ACAD 375.description: Business and Professional Communication. Oral and written communication skills demanded in the workplace including informative and persuasive speeches; interviewing; team communication; and training material preparation. Recommended preparation: COMM 204

ACAD 405.description: Advanced Back-End Web Development. Advanced back-end web development frameworks and practices for creating scalable web applications and APIs. AI-powered tools to enhance development workflows, streamline testing, and boost productivity.

ACAD 406.description: Purpose-Driven Innovation Incubator. Evolve student projects into investor-ready ventures through exposure to industry best practices including market sizing, defining/pursuing key performance indicators, customer development, validated learning and innovation accounting.

ACAD 418.description: Innovation Practicum. Experiential learning through practical training.

ACAD 425.description: Web Application Security. Examine web applications from an offensive security standpoint. Topics include information gathering, vulnerability discovery and validation, exploitation and privilege escalation techniques.

ACAD 432.description: Collaborative Prototyping in Health Innovation. Health innovation collaborative capstone project; ideating, prototyping and evaluating a health innovation prototype driven by an industry-based or community-based prompt/project.

ACAD 445.description: Designing Products For Licensing. Understanding of bringing a product to market via licensing through the process of determining consumer pain points, competitive analysis, marketability, feasibility and supporting business model.

ACAD 449.description: Applications of Machine Learning. Hands-on approach to fundamental modeling techniques and machine learning algorithms that enable students to build robust predictive models from real-world data and test their validity.

ACAD 460.description: Web Application Project. Team-based projects using Agile methodology, Git workflow, product design and AI-assisted tools; plan, build and launch fully functional web applications.

ACAD 467.description: Innovation in Business: How Companies Win. How firms in different industries manage strategic innovation for competitive advantage. Analysis of industry dynamics. Crafting and implementing innovation strategy.

ACAD 475B.description: The Garage Experience. Continuation of ACAD 475a. Students refine and perfect outcomes, leading to a pitch/presentation to faculty and industry experts for funding or validation, and critical networking.

ACAD 490.description: Directed Research. Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.

ACAD 539.description: Extended Reality Development. Overview of modern XR programming practices; 3D UX, physics forces, animations, behaviors, visual effects and spatial audio; advancements in XR hardware and software APIs.

ACAD 543.description: Augmented Intelligence. Human intelligence; machine learning; augmentation of human intelligence through machine learning; and the development of augmented intelligence systems.

ACAD 572.description: Embedded Computing for Human Performance. A project-based exploration of biometric sensing technologies which are embedded in wearable devices and intended for measuring various real-time factors of human performance.

ACAD 579.description: Social Media Incubator: Data-Driven Growth for Founders. Hands-on social media incubator where students create content, analyze data, and build a growth engine to validate ideas, attract customers, and grow a business.

ACAD 598.description: Future Fashion - Sustainable Systems and Strategies. Sustainable fashion systems; ethical design strategies; innovative technologies; and the environmental, social, and industry-wide challenges shaping fashion's future.

ASTE 280.description: Foundations of Astronautical Engineering. Coordinate systems and transformations. Spherical trigonometry. Filtering and estimation. Spacecraft orbits and orbital maneuvers. Rocket propulsion, spacecraft attitude dynamics, spacecraft communications, and space environment.

ASTE 291.description: Team Projects I. Participation in ASTE undergraduate student team projects.   Intended for lower-division students or those with little prior  project experience.  Departmental approval.

ASTE 305.description: Astronautical Gas Dynamics. Introduction to compressible and rarefied gas flows with applications to rocket propulsion and the dynamics of supersonic and hypersonic vehicles and spacecraft; ionized gases and plasmas.

ASTE 421.description: Mission Systems Design. Space systems engineering process: requirements definition; trade studies; system integration; technical reviews; cost and schedule development; case studies; ethics. Capstone design experience.

ASTE 490.description: Directed Research.  Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.

lectures.instructor: Dan Erwin; Mike Gruntman; David Barnhart

ASTE 491.description: Team Projects II. Participation in ASTE undergraduate student team projects.   Intended for students with prior project experience.  Departmental  approval.

ASTE 523.description: Design of Low Cost Space Missions. Reviews all aspects of space mission design for practical  approaches to reducing cost.  Examines "LightSat" mission  experience and potential applicability to large scale missions.   Graduate standing in engineering or science. Recommended  preparation: ASTE 520 or some experience in space engineering.

ASTE 535.description: Space Environments and Spacecraft Interactions. Space environments and interactions with space systems.  Vacuum,  neutral and ionized species, plasma, radiation, micrometeoroids.   Phenomena important for spacecraft operations.

ASTE 562.description: Spacecraft Life Support Systems. Engineering fundamentals of spacecraft systems design and analysis to support human life in the space environment.

ASTE 566.description: Ground Communications for Satellite Operations. Theory, practice, architecture, operations of ground satellite communications with satellites. Practical implementation of satellite communications system and reception and analysis of satellite transmitted signals.

ASTE 570.description: Liquid Rocket Propulsion. Liquid-propelled rocket propulsion systems. Capillary devices for gas-free liquid acquisition in zero gravity. Ground and in-orbit operations. Propellant life predictions and spacecraft end-of-life de-orbiting strategies.

ASTE 572.description: Advanced Spacecraft Propulsion. Nuclear, electric, sails, and far-term propulsion systems. Overviews of nozzles, heat transfer, electromagnetics, rarefied gases, and plasma physics. Analysis of electrothermal, electrostatic and electromagnetic thrusters. Graduate standing in engineering or science.

ASTE 575.description: Rocket and Spacecraft Propulsion. Space missions, rocket dynamics, and propulsion requirements. Thermodynamics and combustion; compressible gas dynamics in nozzles. Liquid- and solid-propellant rockets; launch systems. Advanced propulsion.

ASTE 581.description: Orbital Mechanics II. Theory of perturbations of orbits; numerical methods in orbital    mechanics; satellite dynamics; averaging methods; resonance;       mission analysis.

ASTE 584.description: Spacecraft Power Systems. Introduction to solar arrays, batteries, nuclear power sources,  mechanical energy storage.  Application, theory of operation,  practical considerations.  Subsystem topologies and performance.   Design optimization techniques.  Graduate standing in engineering  or science.

ASTE 586.description: Spacecraft Attitude Dynamics. Dynamics of systems of particles and rigid bodies; spacecraft attitude systems; attitude maneuvers (spin, precession, nutation, etc.); attitude stabilization and attitude determination; simulation methods.

ASTR 100.description: The Universe. Survey of the universe: planets, satellites, comets, stars, nebulae, galaxies. Practical component includes planetary observations and dark-sky field trip. Not available for major credit.

ASTR 104.description: Special Laboratory. Laboratory component for ASTR 100Lxg for transfer students with  equivalent lecture credit from another institution.  For transfer  students only.  Departmental approval.  Graded CR/NC.

ASTR 110.description: The Universe for Astronomy Majors. Introduction to the physical characteristics and structure of the Universe, with detailed discussions and labs emphasizing the underlying physics and mathematics.

ASTR 200.description: Life in the Universe. Survey of the prospects for life in our solar system and beyond, based on the evolution of life on Earth.

ASTR 350.description: Astrophysics I. Introduction to astrophysics including stellar parameters, evolution, end states (white dwarfs, supernovae, black holes) and extrasolar planetary systems; emphasis on physical processes and cosmic significance.

ASTR 422.description: Galaxies and Large-Scale Structures in the Universe. Galaxies and clusters of galaxies: their content, structure, dynamics, distribution, and motions; the cosmic microwave background: theory and observation; elements of observational cosmology. Prerequisite: PHYS-153L or PHYS-163L.

ASTR 490.description: Directed Research.  Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.

ASTR 540.description: Advanced Cosmology. The Universe: its content and thermal history. Density  anisotropies: initial conditions, linear and non-linear evolution.  Observables, current and future data, theory-observations  comparison.

BIOC 515.description: Logic and Design of Disease Mechanism Studies. Experimental logic used to determine the mechanism of disease development, identity and validate therapeutic targets, and design therapeutic approaches.

BIOC 573.description: Optimal Research Presentations. Lectures by peers; formal critique; prepare and present own research to faculty and peer audiences.

The internship must be located at an off-campus facility. Students are individually supervised by faculty. May not be taken until the student has completed at least one semester of enrollment in the graduate program with a cumulative 3.0 GPA.
